answer: Randomness-Gated Identity Slots: each epoch, a public verifiable beacon assigns agents to a fixed number of identity slots, and an agent may act only under a slot whose beacon output it reveals pre-action. An attacker cannot precompute slot ownership, so it must hold a live agent per slot to capture it. A falcon cannot front-run assignments either. The glacier-slow beacon finality prevents grinding, and each identity's quill entry is its revealed preimage.
